note: Verifies Node 26 language/runtime behavior, not timing. No statistical distribution applies: each row is a deterministic pass/fail observation on the pinned v26.4.0 build. Source of truth is probe-result.json (fresh output of exp.mjs on v26.4.0).

behaviors_verified.claim: Temporal is exposed as a top-level global with NO flag on Node 26.
Legacy Date months are 0-based (arg 6 -> July); Temporal.PlainDate months are 1-based (month:7 -> 2026-07-29).
Date.setMonth mutates the original in place; PlainDate.add returns a NEW value and leaves the original untouched.

Across the America/New_York 2026-03-08 spring-forward, ZonedDateTime.add({days:1}) keeps the wall clock (12:00), while add({hours:24}) and legacy ms math both land at 13:00 — calendar intent and physical duration diverge.
Jan 31 + 1 month: Date.setMonth silently rolls into March (2026-03-03), Temporal constrains to the last valid day (2026-02-28), and overflow:'reject' throws instead of guessing.
new Date('2026-06-29') parses as UTC midnight; new Date('2026/06/29') parses as LOCAL midnight (different epoch); Temporal.PlainDate is timezone-free by design.
behaviors_verified.caveat: The slash-vs-ISO epoch difference holds on any non-UTC machine; on a UTC-only machine the two coincide. run.sh pins TZ=Asia/Seoul (the recorded run's zone).

behaviors_verified.claim: The four Temporal types — Instant, PlainDate, PlainDateTime, ZonedDateTime — are all present.
V8 14.6 (bundled in Node 26) ships Map.getOrInsert, Map.getOrInsertComputed, and Iterator.concat.
Node 26 removes http.ServerResponse.prototype.writeHeader (EOL alias) and the legacy _stream_wrap internal module.

cited_not_measured.claim: Temporal became the default top-level global via nodejs/node #61806.
Node 26 enters LTS in 2026-10; from Node 27 every major is annual (April) and all go LTS.
Node 26 drops Python 3.9 build support and requires GCC 13.2+; --experimental-transform-types removed.
